```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# This vignette never connects to a database during package checks or builds.
# Enter benchmark measurements in vignettes/benchmark-results.csv, or run
# tools/benchmarks/flights-vignette-benchmark.R to generate that file.
drivers <- c("RSqlClientNET", "odbc", "RODBCDBI", "RODBC")
template <- expand.grid(driver = drivers, operation = c("write", "read"),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
template$seconds <- NA_real_
template$n_rows <- NA_integer_
template$repetitions <- NA_integer_
results_file <- "benchmark-results.csv"
results <- if (file.exists(results_file)) {
  read.csv(results_file, na.strings = c("", "NA"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
} else {
  template
}
stopifnot(all(c("driver", "operation", "seconds", "n_rows") %in% names(results)))
results$seconds <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(results$seconds))
results$n_rows <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(results$n_rows))

show_results <- function(operation) {
  x <- results[results$operation == operation, , drop = FALSE]
  x <- x[!duplicated(x$driver), , drop = FALSE]
  x <- x[match(drivers, x$driver), , drop = FALSE]
  baseline <- x$seconds[match("odbc", x$driver)]
  # Compute ratios only when both times were actually measured and positive.
  speedup <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(x))
  if (length(baseline) == 1L && is.finite(baseline) && baseline > 0) {
    valid <- is.finite(x$seconds) & x$seconds > 0
    speedup[valid] <- baseline / x$seconds[valid]
  }
  format_s <- function(z) ifelse(is.finite(z), sprintf("%.3f", z), "—")
  data <- data.frame(
    Driver = drivers,
    `Elapsed (s)` = format_s(x$seconds),
    `Rows` = ifelse(is.finite(x$n_rows), format(x$n_rows, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), "—"),
    `Speed vs. odbc` = ifelse(is.finite(speedup) & speedup > 0,
                             sprintf("%.2f×", speedup), "—"),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  # Explicit HTML output avoids Markdown being collapsed into one paragraph.
  knitr::kable(
    data,
    format = "html",
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
    caption = if (operation == "write") "Writing to SQL Server" else "Reading from SQL Server",
    table.attr = 'class="rscn-benchmark-table"',
    escape = TRUE
  )
}
```

## Overview

This vignette compares reading and writing **Microsoft SQL Server** tables using
[RSqlClientNET](https://github.com/tsp/RSqlClientNET),
[odbc](https://odbc.r-dbi.org/articles/benchmarks.html), `RODBCDBI`, and `RODBC`.
Its structure is inspired by the [odbc benchmarks vignette](https://odbc.r-dbi.org/articles/benchmarks.html),
but these are *new* measurements, not the historical timings from that page.

The tables below display the values from `benchmark-results.csv`. Until you
run the comparison, unmeasured values are shown as dashes rather than
invented timings. You may edit the CSV directly or generate it with the
accompanying script. The vignette can be built without a SQL Server or
credentials.

The comparison measures elapsed wall-clock time, not just CPU time. Drivers
must connect to the *same* SQL Server instance and database, from the *same*
client machine. Connection setup, test-data generation, row-count verification,
and cleanup are **excluded** from the timed sections.

## Setup

To remain comparable with the original `odbc` vignette, we use
`nycflights13::flights`, converted from tibble to `data.frame`, and omit the
`time_hour` column. The data contain `r if (requireNamespace("nycflights13", quietly = TRUE)) format(nrow(nycflights13::flights), big.mark = ",") else "336,776"`
rows and 18 columns after removal of that timestamp column.

```{r data-preparation, eval=FALSE}
flights <- as.data.frame(nycflights13::flights)
flights$time_hour <- NULL
stopifnot(ncol(flights) == 18L)
```

The runner connects to SQL Server with the existing RSqlClientNET connection
string and an ODBC DSN. The examples below use Windows Authentication and the
`SqlClientRTest` DSN; no username or password is stored in the repository.
All drivers must reach the same SQL Server instance and database.
`RODBC` and `RODBCDBI` are optional because their older interfaces have
different capabilities and setup requirements.

```{r connect-example, eval=FALSE}
library(DBI)

con_sqlclient <- DBI::dbConnect(
  RSqlClientNET::SqlClientNET(),
  connection_string = Sys.getenv("RSQLCLIENTNET_TEST_CONNECTION_STRING"),
  data_table = FALSE   # DBI-compatible data.frame result
)

con_odbc <- DBI::dbConnect(
  odbc::odbc(),
  dsn = Sys.getenv("RSQLCLIENTNET_BENCH_DSN", unset = "SqlClientRTest")
)

# Disconnect when finished:
DBI::dbDisconnect(con_sqlclient)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con_odbc)
```

## Writing

Each driver uploads the *same* `flights` data to a new, driver-specific table.
The write timer includes table creation and data upload, using `dbWriteTable()`
for the DBI drivers and `RODBC::sqlSave()` for RODBC. The table is checked and
deleted after the timer has stopped. Repetitions run in randomized order to
reduce systematic warm-up effects. A single manually timed write would look
like this (the accompanying runner repeats and verifies it automatically):

```{r write-example, eval=FALSE}
write_time <- system.time(
  DBI::dbWriteTable(con_sqlclient, "rscn_bench_write", flights,
                    row.names = FALSE)
)[["elapsed"]]
DBI::dbRemoveTable(con_sqlclient, "rscn_bench_write")
```

```{r writing-results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(paste(as.character(show_results("write")), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n", sep = "")
```

## Reading

A single common `flights` table is populated with RSqlClientNET *before*
measurement. Each backend reads that same table using `dbReadTable()` or
`RODBC::sqlFetch()`. The elapsed time includes fetching and materializing an
R result, but not preparing the SQL table. Each result is checked for the
expected number of rows and columns.

```{r read-example, eval=FALSE}
# Set up a common table once, before timing any reads:
DBI::dbWriteTable(con_sqlclient, "rscn_bench_read", flights,
                  row.names = FALSE)
read_time <- system.time(
  result <- DBI::dbReadTable(con_odbc, "rscn_bench_read")
)[["elapsed"]]
stopifnot(nrow(result) == nrow(flights))
DBI::dbRemoveTable(con_sqlclient, "rscn_bench_read")
```

```{r reading-results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(paste(as.character(show_results("read")), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n", sep = "")
```

`Speed vs. odbc` is computed as `odbc elapsed / driver elapsed`; values above
1.00× indicate faster execution than `odbc` *for that operation and setup*.
Blank values mean no result has been entered. The comparison does not imply
that one driver will be faster across all SQL types or workloads.

## Enter your results

Edit `vignettes/benchmark-results.csv` and replace the empty `seconds` values
with your measured median elapsed times. Fill in `n_rows` and `repetitions` if
available. Do not enter numbers from the historical odbc webpage, since they
were measured on a different system and with different software versions.

Alternatively, from the project root run:

```{r run-example, eval=FALSE}
# `con_str` is your existing trusted Windows Authentication connection string.
Sys.setenv(
  RSQLCLIENTNET_TEST_CONNECTION_STRING = con_str,
  RSQLCLIENTNET_BENCH_DSN = "SqlClientRTest",
  RSQLCLIENTNET_BENCH_EXTRA_DRIVERS = "RODBCDBI,RODBC",
  RSQLCLIENTNET_VIGNETTE_REPEATS = 5
)
# Clear optional connection-string overrides so the runner uses the DSN.
Sys.unsetenv(c("ODBC_CONNECTION_STRING", "RSQLCLIENTNET_BENCH_ODBC_CONNECTION_STRING"))
source("tools/benchmarks/flights-vignette-benchmark.R")
result <- run_flights_vignette_benchmark()

# Rebuild the HTML vignette after collecting results:
rmarkdown::render("vignettes/benchmarks.Rmd", quiet = TRUE)
```

The runner defaults to three repetitions and compares RSqlClientNET and
`odbc`; the example above requests five repetitions and includes the optional
`RODBC` / `RODBCDBI` drivers using the same DSN.
It overwrites the CSV template with the newly measured medians, and prints
all attempts in the console. To inspect variability, increase the repetition
count or retain the per-attempt CSV written alongside the medians.

## Interpretation and reproducibility

Benchmarks are highly sensitive to operating system, R version, driver
version, network latency, SQL Server configuration, SQL table types, and
caching. Report these alongside the timings. In particular:

- RSqlClientNET uses its default native **columnar** read transport and
  default read batch size (32,768 rows in v0.1.0).
- All DBI drivers return an ordinary `data.frame` for this benchmark;
  RSqlClientNET's optional `data_table = TRUE` is **not** enabled.
- The timestamp column is excluded to match the published odbc vignette.
  For performance involving SQL Server `datetime` / `datetime2` and timezones,
  use the separate `tools/benchmarks/datetime-local-binary.R` benchmark.
- These operations use SQL Server tables, not R-only serialization or local
  synthetic data frames; connection establishment and test data setup are
  outside the timers.
- `RODBC` and `RODBCDBI` have older APIs and may be unavailable or reject
  particular data types. Missing measurements should remain blank rather than
  being treated as zero.

**Source and methodology:** [odbc benchmarks](https://odbc.r-dbi.org/articles/benchmarks.html).
This vignette is maintained as part of RSqlClientNET; it does not incorporate
timing claims from that earlier benchmark.


## Bulk insert, TableLock and SQL Server transaction logging

`dbWriteTable()` and `dbAppendTable()` support an explicit `table_lock = TRUE` argument, which maps to `SqlBulkCopyOptions.TableLock` for that operation only (`FALSE` by default). Locking can reduce performance in concurrent systems, so it is intentionally opt-in. SQL Server can use **minimal logging** for eligible bulk operations under SIMPLE/BULK_LOGGED recovery, subject to table/index structure and additional engine conditions. Do not assume this applies to indexed tables or databases using FULL recovery.

In an October 2026 developer test (SQL Server 2025 Express, SIMPLE, empty disposable VARCHAR(MAX) heap), the median elapsed time for 50,000 values was 9.33 s with `table_lock = FALSE`, 5.61 s with `table_lock = TRUE`, and 13.45 s for standard `odbc` append (five repeats). Logically generated transaction log bytes were about 140 MB and 5.38 MB respectively for the RSqlClientNET alternatives. These measurements are workload-specific and should not be generalized to production.

For reproducible comparisons of SQL transaction behavior, use `tools/benchmarks/benchmark-bulk-transactions.R`. The `result$logical_log` values come from **separately** instrumented writes with an explicit DBI transaction, read before commit. Physical file I/O is database-wide rather than per-transaction; sums of wait times may include parallel workers. `tools/benchmarks/benchmark-create-vs-append.R` independently compares creation and append workflows, including a precreated indexed table. Tests must run only on disposable databases.
